text: Fill in each blank with the correct term from the section on body water and electrolytes.
questions: Total body water in a 70 kg man is about 42 L, with two-thirds in the *intracellular:Which compartment holds the larger share of body water?* fluid and one-third in the extracellular fluid.
The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase maintains ionic gradients by pumping three sodium ions out and two *potassium:Which cation is concentrated inside cells?* ions into each cell.
Sodium is the main extracellular cation, balanced primarily by chloride and *bicarbonate:Name the two principal extracellular anions.*.
Normal plasma *osmolality/Osmolality* is 285–295 mOsm/kg, and a change in serum sodium usually signals a change in water balance.
Within red blood cells, *haemoglobin/hemoglobin* is the dominant buffer.

overallFeedback.feedback: The body keeps two-thirds of its water inside cells (ICF, K⁺-rich) and one-third outside (ECF, Na⁺-rich). Cell membranes separate ICF from ECF, and the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase maintains their Na⁺ and K⁺ gradients. Sodium sets osmolality, bicarbonate is the main ECF buffer, and proteins and phosphate buffer intracellular fluid; haemoglobin dominates buffering within red cells.
